**Expert Insights**  
- Baseline data is established after installation and post-maintenance for critical parameters: bearing temperatures (highest point), balance readings, vibration analysis, and motion amplification data, all under normal operating conditions.
- Condition-Based Maintenance (CBM) monitoring uses a site CBM Matrix:
  - Vibration analysis per STD-ENG-015, with readings on horizontal, axial, and vertical planes, and historical trending for early fault diagnosis.
  - Ultrasound monitoring for bearing condition, especially during lubrication routes.
  - Audio-Visual Inspection (AVI) routes at frequencies set by the CBM Matrix.
  - Thermography (Tier 2 hot spot detection) during AVI routines, providing non-invasive temperature monitoring.
  - Motion amplification technology (corporate investment, held at Wissington) for visualizing vibration sources, especially high 1x frequencies, looseness, and soft foot faults; baseline surveys upon fan installation and recommended 5-yearly surveys on established plant, conducted at 30x magnification from consistent geographic locations for repeatability.
- Laser alignment equipment (ANSI/ASA S2.75-2017/part 1) is used upon installation and post-maintenance with precision tolerances: 0.1mm angular/0.13mm offset for up to 1000 RPM, 0.08mm angular/0.07mm offset for up to 2000 RPM, and 0.07mm angular/0.07mm offset for up to 3000 RPM. The equipment provides intuitive feedback—a "smiley face/OK" indicates acceptable alignment.
- Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) suite for critical fan inspections:
  - Liquid dye penetrant (BS EN 10228-2:2016) for non-magnetic components
  - Magnetic particle inspection (BS EN 10228-1:2016) for magnetic materials
  - Eddy current inspection (BS EN ISO 15549:2019) for coated surfaces
  - All performed by Level 2 certified personnel minimum
- Routine inspections:
  - Daily: Monitor temperature thresholds (above 40°C for casings, above 80°C for motors/gearboxes/bearings), oil leaks, abnormal noise, equipment condition
  - Bi-weekly: Internal inspections for conveying systems (STD-ENG-004)
- Data interpretation:
  - DIPF (Design, Installation, Potential Failure, Failure) curve used to interpret equipment lifespan and guide maintenance to maximize mean time to failure and minimize repair costs
  - Trending and quantitative analysis: All CBM equipment captures quantitative data, building historical profiles for early fault diagnosis and issue development tracking
- KPI-based monitoring for process quality:
  - Thick juice storage: pH, degree of saturation, and temperature monitored as KPIs
  - Samples analyzed per STD-OSS-008 every two weeks at multiple tank depths
- The key advantage of these advanced tools is their ability to detect issues in the "Potential Failure" phase of the DIPF curve, allowing proactive intervention before catastrophic failures.
- Overall approach shifts from reactive to proactive maintenance by using data to predict and prevent failures.
